essays.stem: Describe how you would set up a computer workstation so that you can work for long periods without pain or strain.
essays.modelAnswer: First I adjust the chair so my feet are flat on the floor or on a footrest, my knees are about level with my hips and my lower back is supported. I place the screen straight in front of me, about an arm's length away, with the top of the screen at or a little below eye level. I tilt or move it to cut glare from windows and lights. I put the keyboard and mouse close, so my elbows stay near my body and my wrists stay straight. I keep things I use often within easy reach. I keep cables tidy and off the walkway, and drinks away from the computer. While working I take short breaks, stand and stretch, and look at something far away from time to time to rest my eyes. If I still feel pain, I tell my supervisor.
markingPoints: Chair adjusted: feet flat, knees about level with hips, back supported
Screen straight ahead, about an arm's length away, top at or just below eye level, no glare
Keyboard and mouse close, elbows by the body, wrists straight
Short regular breaks, stretching and resting the eyes
Tidy cables, no drinks near the computer, report any pain

essays.stem: Explain how you would organise work files into folders on a computer for a small business, such as a fabrication shop or a villa, and why this matters.
essays.modelAnswer: I would make one main folder for the business, then folders inside it for each kind of work. For a fabrication shop these could be Quotations, Invoices, Job sheets and Staff rosters. For a villa they could be Bookings, Housekeeping and Supplies. Inside these I can make folders by year or by month. I give every file a clear name that says what it is and the date, such as "Quote - Campbell gate - 2026-10-12", and never names like "Document1". I save each file straight into the right folder, and I remove old copies so there is only one up-to-date version. I back up the main folder to a USB drive or online storage. This matters because anyone can find a file quickly, files are not lost or mixed up, customers get the right papers and no time is wasted searching.
markingPoints: One main folder with sub-folders for each type of work, with suitable examples
Sub-folders by year or month
Clear file names that say what the file is and give the date
Save in the right place, keep one current version, and back up
Reason: files are found quickly, not lost or mixed up, and time is saved

essays.stem: Describe the steps to create, format, save and print a one-page notice telling staff about a safety meeting.
essays.modelAnswer: I open the word processor and start a new blank document. I type the notice: a heading such as "Safety Meeting", then the day, date, time and place, who must attend and what to bring. I select the heading and make it bold, larger and centred so it stands out. I choose a clear font for the rest, about 12 to 14 point, and use bullet points for the main facts. I run the spelling check and then read it through myself, checking the date and time are right. I save the file in the correct folder with a clear name, such as "Safety meeting notice - Nov 2026". I use Print Preview to check that it fits on one page. Then I choose the printer and the number of copies, and print. I check the printout and put it up on the notice board.
markingPoints: Start a new document and type the content: what, when, where and who
Format the heading (bold, larger, centred) and keep the body text clear, for example with bullet points
Spell check and proofread, checking the facts
Save with a clear name in the right folder
Print Preview, choose printer and copies, print and check the printout

essays.stem: Explain how you would set up a simple spreadsheet to list supplies with their quantities, prices and a grand total.
essays.modelAnswer: I open a new spreadsheet. In row 1 I type the headings: Item in A1, Quantity in B1, Unit price (J$) in C1 and Cost in D1, and I make them bold. From row 2 down I type one item on each row, for example boxes of welding rods or bottles of floor cleaner, with the quantity and the price of one unit. In D2 I type the formula =B2*C2 to work out the cost, then copy it down the column for every item. Under the last item I type "Total" and use =SUM to add up the Cost column. I format the money cells as currency with two decimal places and widen the columns so everything shows. I check a few answers with a calculator. I save the file with a clear name. If a price changes later, the cost and the total update by themselves.
markingPoints: Headings in the first row (item, quantity, unit price, cost)
One item per row with its quantity and unit price
A multiply formula such as =B2*C2, copied down the column
A SUM formula for the grand total
Money cells formatted, columns widened, answers checked and the file saved

essays.stem: Describe how to write and send a clear, polite work email with an attachment, for example a quotation for a customer.
essays.modelAnswer: I open the email program and choose New message. In the To box I type the customer's email address carefully, and I put my supervisor in CC if they need a copy. I write a short subject line that says what the email is about, such as "Quotation for burglar bars – 14 Hope Road". I begin with a greeting, like "Good morning Mrs Grant". In a few short, polite sentences I say what is attached and anything important, such as the price, how long it is valid and how to reply. I end politely and add my name, job title and phone number. I click Attach, find the quotation file and add it, then check that the right file is there. I read the whole email again for spelling, tone and the correct address. Then I click Send and check that it is in the Sent folder.
markingPoints: Correct email address in To, and CC for anyone who needs a copy
Clear subject line
Greeting, short polite message, and a sign-off with name and contact details
Attach the correct file and check it is there
Proofread, send, and check the Sent folder

essays.stem: Explain how a worker can keep work files and customer information safe on a computer that several people share.
essays.modelAnswer: Each worker should log on with their own account and a strong password that is long and mixes letters, numbers and symbols. The password should never be written on a note by the screen or told to anyone. When leaving the desk, even for a short time, the worker should lock the screen, and log off at the end of the shift. Customer details, such as a guest's phone number or a customer's address, should be saved only in the right folders, not on the desktop or on a personal USB drive. Antivirus software and system updates should be kept up to date. The worker should not open strange emails, links or attachments, and should not plug in an unknown USB drive. Important files should be backed up. Any problem, such as a lost USB drive or a possible scam, should be reported to the supervisor at once.
markingPoints: Own account with a strong password that is kept secret
Lock the screen when away and log off at the end of the shift
Keep customer information only where it belongs, not on the desktop or personal drives
Antivirus and updates kept current; no strange links, attachments or unknown USB drives
Back up important files and report problems at once

essays.stem: Describe how you would search the internet for work information, such as prices from local suppliers, and how you would check that the information can be trusted.
essays.modelAnswer: First I decide exactly what I need, for example the price of a 6 m length of 25 mm square steel tube, or of a case of bath towels, from suppliers in Jamaica. I open a web browser and type a few clear keywords into a search engine, such as "square tube steel supplier Kingston". I look at the results and open the websites of real businesses. I check that each site gives an address, a phone number and a recent date, and that prices are in Jamaican dollars and say whether GCT is included. I compare at least two or three suppliers. I am careful with adverts and with offers that look far too cheap. Where I can, I call the supplier to confirm the price and that they have stock. I write down the details, with the website address and the date, and give them to my supervisor.
markingPoints: Decide exactly what information is needed
Use a browser and a search engine with a few clear keywords
Check the source: real business, contact details, recent date, J$ prices and whether GCT is included
Compare more than one supplier and be wary of offers that look too good
Confirm by phone where possible, record the details and report to the supervisor

essays.stem: A printer in the office will not print your document. Describe the checks you would make, in order, and say when you would report the problem.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check that I sent the job to the right printer, because the computer may be set to a different one. Then I look at the printer: is it switched on, and does its screen or a light show an error? I check that the power cable and the USB or network cable are pushed in firmly, or that it is connected to the Wi-Fi. I check that there is paper in the tray and that no paper is jammed. If there is a jam, I switch off and follow the maker's instructions to pull the paper out gently. I check the ink or toner level. Then I look at the print queue on the computer, and if a job is stuck I cancel it and try again. If none of this works, or the printer shows a fault I do not understand, I stop. I do not open the inside of the printer, and I report it to my supervisor.
markingPoints: Check the right printer was chosen
Check power, cables or network connection, and any error light
Check paper, and clear a jam safely following the maker's instructions
Check ink or toner and the print queue
Report to the supervisor if it still fails; do not attempt repairs inside the printer

essays.stem: Compare saving work files on the computer's own drive, on a USB flash drive, and in online (cloud) storage. Give one good point and one weak point of each.
essays.modelAnswer: Saving on the computer's own drive is quick and works without the internet, so it is good for everyday work. Its weak point is that if the computer breaks, is stolen or gets a virus, the files can be lost, and other workers cannot reach them from another place. A USB flash drive is small and cheap, and it lets me carry files from the office to the workshop or to another computer. But it is easy to lose or damage, it can carry a virus from one computer to another, and anyone who finds it can read the files. Online or cloud storage keeps a copy away from the building, so the files are safe if the computer fails, and the team can open them from different places. Its weak points are that it needs an internet connection and a strong password. The safest plan is to keep important work in more than one place.
markingPoints: Own drive: quick and needs no internet, but files are lost if the computer fails or is stolen
USB flash drive: easy to carry, but easily lost or damaged and can spread viruses
Cloud storage: kept off-site and shared easily, but needs internet and a secure log-in
Keep important work in more than one place (backup)

essays.stem: Describe how to keep computer equipment clean and in good working order in a workplace such as a site office or a villa front desk.
essays.modelAnswer: Before cleaning, I shut down the computer and switch it off at the wall. I wipe the screen gently with a soft, dry, lint-free cloth. I do not spray liquid straight onto the screen or use rough paper. I clean the keyboard and mouse with a slightly damp cloth or a wipe made for electronics, and I turn the keyboard over to shake out crumbs. I keep the air vents clear so the computer does not overheat, and I keep it out of direct sun and away from dust. In a workshop the computer should stay in the office, away from grinding dust and the welding bays. Nobody should eat or drink at the computer. A surge protector helps, because power cuts and lightning can damage equipment. I keep cables tidy and never pull on them. I report damage, strange noises or overheating to the supervisor instead of opening the case.
markingPoints: Shut down and switch off at the wall before cleaning
Use the right cleaning method: soft dry cloth for the screen, no liquid sprayed on it
Keep vents clear; keep the computer away from heat, sun, dust and workshop grinding or welding
No food or drink; tidy cables; use a surge protector
Report faults instead of opening the case

practical1.title: Create, format and print a one-page work notice in a word processor
practical1.brief: As a group, produce a one-page notice for staff at a workplace. Choose one from the assessor's scenario cards: a weekly work roster for a fabrication shop, or a cleaning roster for a villa. The notice must have a bold, centred heading, a short paragraph, a table with at least 4 rows (for example day, task, person and time) and the business name and date at the bottom. Share the work so that each member does at least one stage at the computer while the others watch and check: (1) make a group folder and start a new document, (2) type the text, (3) format the heading and the text, (4) insert and fill in the table, (5) check the spelling, use Print Preview, save with a clear file name and print. In a group of 4, one member does two stages. Each member then tells the assessor what they did. Photograph the screen at each stage and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the printed notice once for the whole group.
materials: A computer with a word processor, connected to a printer
A scenario card with the roster details (fabrication shop or villa)
The Centre's shared folder or a USB flash drive
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The workstation set up safely, with the group around it
The new group folder and the blank document
The heading formatted bold and centred, and the table filled in
The Print Preview screen showing one page
The Save As window showing the file name and the folder
The printed notice held up next to the screen
checklist: Set up the chair, screen and keyboard safely before starting
Made the group folder and saved the file there with a clear name
Typed accurately, using Enter, Shift and the space bar correctly
Formatted the heading (bold, larger, centred) and kept the body text clear
Inserted a table with the right number of columns and filled it in
Checked the spelling and proofread the notice
Used Print Preview and printed one correct copy
Explained clearly to the assessor what they did at their stage
Logged off and left the workstation tidy
safety: Keep drinks and food away from the computer
Keep cables off the floor where people walk
Sit with good posture and take a short break if working for a long time
Do not open unknown files or plug in unknown USB drives

practical2.title: Build a supplies cost list in a spreadsheet and send it by email
practical2.brief: As a group, make a spreadsheet that lists at least 8 supplies for a workplace, with the quantity, the price of one unit in J$, the cost of each line and a grand total. Use the price list the assessor gives you (for example welding rods, gloves and grinding discs, or towels, soap and cleaning liquid). Each member does at least one stage at the computer while the others check: (1) type the headings and the items, (2) enter the quantities and prices, (3) write the cost formula and copy it down, (4) add the SUM total and format the money cells, (5) save the file and attach it to an email to the assessor, with a clear subject line and a short polite message. In a group of 4, one member does two stages. Before sending, change one price to show that the total updates by itself. Photograph the screen at each stage and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: A computer with a spreadsheet program, internet, and an email account set up by the Centre
A printed price list from the assessor
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The headings and the item list typed in
The cost formula showing in the formula bar
The SUM total, with the money cells formatted as currency
The total after one price was changed
The email with the subject line and the file attached, before sending
The Sent folder showing that the email went
checklist: Set up the workstation safely and sat correctly
Typed the headings and data into the correct cells
Wrote a correct multiply formula starting with =
Copied the formula down without errors
Used SUM correctly for the grand total
Formatted the money cells and widened the columns so all figures show
Checked at least two answers with a calculator
Saved the file with a clear name in the right folder
Wrote a polite email with a clear subject and the right file attached
safety: Keep drinks and food away from the computer
Keep cables tidy and off the walkway
Use only the Centre's email account for this task and never share a password
Take a short break and rest your eyes if working for a long time
